rationale.idea: Replace same-validation-set epoch argmax with a held-out-user comparison of fixed checkpoint-combination rules on the incumbent FM training trajectory.
rationale.why_expected_to_help: The current evidence against snapshot/checkpoint averaging is explicitly low-confidence and potentially biased because the winner was chosen and scored on the same validation set; held-out-user rule testing can detect whether averaging nearby good epochs reduces variance without merely overfitting validation users. Use it whenever a choice is being made using the same data it will be judged on.' Also grounded in the measured single-model checkpoint signal from research memory: checkpoint combination was previously near-neutral to mildly positive in one seed (0.6040 vs 0.6038, inside noise), so the uncertainty is specifically about selection methodology rather than a clearly dead mechanism.

code_summary: The script trains one incumbent numpy FM configuration with captured per-epoch validation scores, then implements checkpoint-rule selection as a post-training model-selection problem over users rather than epochs. Existing menu primitives can request checkpoint averaging, but they cannot evaluate whether a selection rule generalises using held-out-user resampling, nor can they choose among alternative fixed rules based on captured epoch predictions. This mechanism is therefore outside the menu: it wraps train_numpy_fm plus selection_rule_test/capture_selection_rule_test logic and emits final scores using the winning rule on validation while safely falling back to the trained model's provided test scores because per-epoch test checkpoints are not exposed by train_lib.
